title: Video Script
description: The narration, annotations and avatar placement for one training module, one entry per Synthesia scene. Stage 2 output, and the artifact Stage 3 builds the Synthesia session from. Scene IDs and capture timings come from capture_map.json and must agree with it.

target_runtime.description: Seconds. A planning input, not an outcome — finished video is capped by the Synthesia credit budget, so an over-budget module gets split before it is built.

capture_map.description: Path to the capture_map.json this script was written against

objectives.description: What a learner should be able to do afterwards. Every keep-scene maps to at least one.

text.description: Behavioural — 'raise a purchase requisition for a stocked item', not 'understand requisitions'

glossary.description: Terminology fixed for the module. Same discipline the proposal skill applies to the client's naming convention: pick the client's term and never drift off it.

avoid.description: Synonyms that must not appear — legacy system names, informal shorthand

wpm_band.description: Words-per-minute range narration is budgeted against. Defaults to [130, 165] — a training pace, slower than conversational.

role.description: Drives the avatar default: visible on intro/transition/outro, hidden on step.

frame_ref.description: The keyframe this scene's narration was written from. Invariant 1: present, or gap is true. There is no third state.

narration.description: What the avatar says over this scene. Written to the word budget derived from the scene's measured duration.

silent.description: A deliberate beat with no narration. Distinct from an unnarrated scene, which is a coverage failure.

gap.description: The frame does not establish what this scene needs to say, and the consultant must fill it in. Renders as a visible placeholder in the build sheet, never as plausible-sounding narration.

gap_note.description: Required when gap is true — what is missing and what the consultant needs to confirm

annotations.description: On-screen callouts. Copy must name the object being acted on, never restate the narration — duplicated text splits attention and teaches nothing.

type.description: highlight = box around a control. callout = short label with a leader. step_counter = 'Step 3 of 7'. lower_third = name/role strip, intro and outro only.

text.description: Required for callout, step_counter and lower_third

target.description: The on-screen control being marked, in the system's own naming

rect.description: [x, y, w, h] as fractions of frame width/height, origin top-left. Required for highlight.

anchor.description: [x, y] as fractions of frame width/height. Where a callout points.

visible.description: Default false on step scenes. A persistent talking head competes with the screen exactly when the learner is following a click path, and it burns credit on every second of runtime.
